title: Meta Stock Analysis: Buy or Sell? (My Final Verdict)
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc gives his final verdict on Meta after earnings, asking whether he will add to or sell a position he counts among his larger holdings. Revenue rose 26% year over year to $64.2 billion, as ad impressions rose 10%, the average price per ad increased, and engagement improved, all delivered with 12% fewer employees — evidence, he argues, that AI-driven targeting and productivity are lifting the core business. The stock first jumped about 4% after hours, then fell as much as 8% the next day. His main concern is the pace of investment: free cash flow turned negative at -$2.1 billion in the quarter, and he models -$10 billion this year, -$41 billion next year and -$3 billion the year after, turning positive only from 2029. The balance sheet shows $82.4 billion of cash and marketable securities against $83.7 billion of debt, with capex over $135 billion this year and an estimated $150–175 billion next year. Other risks he names are dilution and a possible Zuckerberg stock sale for a California billionaire tax. Against that, Q4 revenue is guided to about $74.5 billion at the midpoint, and the Muse personal agent is succeeding before monetisation. His updated DCF is $913, the forward P/E is 21, and he sees 40%+ upside over 12–18 months. The call is META — BUY reiterated, ranked a top-10 best stock to buy. Some figures, including the current price and the exact price-per-ad increase, drop out of the auto-captions.

calls.base_case: Revenue $64.2bn, up 26% YoY; ad impressions +10% with higher price per ad and engagement, delivered with 12% fewer employees; Q4 revenue guided to about $74.5bn at the midpoint.
calls.bull_case: AI-driven ad targeting and productivity are lifting the core business; Muse personal agent is already succeeding (not yet monetised) and management expects >10x serving-efficiency improvement next year from off-peak use, more efficient models and inference optimisation.
calls.bear_case: Free cash flow turned negative (-$2.1bn in the quarter); he now models -$10bn this year, -$41bn next year and -$3bn the year after, positive only from 2029 ($60bn+).
